summary: Learning and inference on time series can pose significant statistical challenges, including autocorrelated observations, distribution shift over time, and the curse of dimensionality. These challenges complicate the practical application of causal discovery algorithms, which already suffer from high computational and sample complexity in the general case.
takeaways: To mitigate these issues, this work introduces Iterative Temporal Parent Discovery (ITPD): a sound and complete constraint-based procedure for causal structure learning on multivariate time series with causal nonstationarity.
ITPD takes a local-to-global learning approach that discovers the global graph by sequentially discovering the parent set for each variable.
With an exact oracle, ITPD performed the least number of tests and used the smallest average conditioning set sizes relative to baselines.
